topic.title: Class 3 graph generation: MC isomers are different from Natural Product not because they are unstable (GFN2-xTB)
topic.forumName: Enveda CASMI 2026 - Molecule ID From Mass Spectra
topic.content:
Hi all. Here is a small experiment on graph generation targeting Class 3.

I first tried DiffMS, then switched to generating molecular graphs directly with Monte Carlo. The overall strategy: map the MS/MS spectrum to a molecular fingerprint (I use a modified FPNet-like model, as in other public notebooks), generate many candidate graphs, and pick those closest to the predicted fingerprint.

The MC starts from known structures with the same formula and jumps between isomers by rewiring bonds. No chemical knowledge or biosynthetic pathways are used. Obviously broken graphs are removed, especially strained ones and those containing ring systems not found in any database.

Mixing these generated candidates with DB candidates (with a score discount) gave only +0.006 to +0.011 on my local validation, and no visible change on the LB.

Hypothesis. Among all isomers that graph enumeration can produce, real molecules occupy a very limited region. To appear in this competition, a molecule must

(1) be stable, (2) be reachable by a biosynthetic pathway, (3) be measurable by MS/MS (ionizes and fragments).

I assumed (3) differs little among isomers of a fixed formula, since ionization efficiency is largely explained by formula-level features such as the numbers of H and N. So I tested (1): are the generated isomers simply unstable?

Setup

250 natural products held out from the training data 1,300 generated structures that reached the top 25, the 250 correct structures, and 10 random registered isomers per formula (2,139) RDKit ETKDG (5 conformers) → lowest MMFF → xtb --gfn 2 --opt, gas phase ΔE = E − median E of registered isomers of the same formula (kcal/mol)

Results

Median ΔE: generated +1.7, registered 0.0, correct −2.7 (SD 19–24) Generated structures ranked above the correct answer were less stable than it in only 55–56% of cases Connectivity changed during optimization for only 0.3% of generated structures

ΔE threshold (kcal/mol) Generated removed Registered removed
> 20 17.0% 15.1%
> 50 5.3% 3.9%

Takeaway. The generated isomers are not particularly unstable, and the correct structure is not the most stable isomer either (around the lower 40% of registered isomers). So (1) does not explain the failure. My guess, not yet tested, is that (2) biosynthetic reachability is what matters.

Cost: about 5.5 h on a Kaggle CPU for 3,689 structures. Caveats: single conformer, gas phase, one validation split.

comments.content: Good post! I think your direction can improve the generalization ability of other models by physically/chemically informed way. But what is the graph transfer rule in MC graph generation? The complete random generation searches all graph space like you said and you should do narrow the transfer candidates.

replies.content:
Thanks for the question!

The MC move is:

  1. Explicit-H graph with fixed valences (C 4, N 3, O 2, S 2, P 3, halogens/H 1) and bond orders 0–3.
  2. Pick two bonds a–b and c–d at random (four distinct atoms), decrease both by 1 and increase a–c and b–d by 1. This keeps the formula and every valence.

Chemically unreasonable graphs are then filtered out, and the walk is accepted by Metropolis on the distance to the fingerprint predicted from the spectrum, so it stays near that point in feature space.

In other words, the isomers this produces are GDB-17-type structures. They are not reached through any biosynthetic route of natural products. Looking at train, larger molecules seem to be built mostly from combinations of known building blocks, so restricting generation to what biosynthetic routes can reach should make the candidates much more natural-product-like.

That is why I moved to a biosynthesis-like proposal: take a DB molecule X, apply a modification M (hydroxylation, methylation, glycosylation/hydrolysis, …) to get Y, and judge the statement "X + M → Y" with the query spectrum, X's library spectrum and the formula. It restricts moves to chemically meaningful ones, and so far it works better than MC for me.
